measures.title: HIV infection screening
measures.population: Adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years; younger/older if increased risk
measures.action: Screen for HIV infection (FDA-approved antigen/antibody immunoassay)
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for HIV infection in adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) Infection: Screening (2019)
measures.appliesReason: Age 43 falls within the 15-65 band; recommendation is universal regardless of risk. At least one-time screening indicated.
measures.notes: Grade A, applies to all adults 15-65 regardless of risk factors. USPSTF does not specify a screening frequency for the general population; clinical judgment / risk-based rescreening. CDC recommends at least once for everyone 13-64.

measures.title: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection screening
measures.population: Adults aged 18 to 79 years
measures.action: Screen for HCV with anti-HCV antibody testing followed by confirmatory testing
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults aged 18 to 79 years.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Hepatitis C Virus Infection in Adolescents and Adults: Screening (2020)
measures.appliesReason: Age 43 falls within the 18-79 universal band; no risk gate required.
measures.notes: Grade B, universal for ages 18-79. One-time screening for most adults; periodic screening only for those with continued risk (e.g., injection drug use). Average-risk patient needs one-time screen if not previously done.

measures.title: Colorectal cancer screening
measures.population: Adults aged 45 to 49 years (B); 50 to 75 (A); 76 to 85 selectively (C)
measures.action: Screen with stool-based test (high-sensitivity), colonoscopy, CT colonography, or flexible sigmoidoscopy
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends screening for colorectal cancer in adults aged 45 to 49 years.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Colorectal Cancer: Screening (2021)
measures.appliesReason: Eligibility begins at age 45 (Grade B); patient is 43, so not yet eligible. Becomes eligible in ~2 years.
measures.notes: Grade B at 45-49, Grade A at 50-75, Grade C (selective) at 76-85. Patient is 43 -> NOT YET ELIGIBLE; flag for activation at age 45. Interval depends on modality (e.g., colonoscopy q10y, FIT annually, FIT-DNA q1-3y, CT colonography q5y, flex sig q5y or q10y with annual FIT) -- USPSTF lists modality-specific intervals rather than a single interval.

measures.title: Prediabetes and type 2 diabetes screening (abnormal blood glucose)
measures.population: Adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity (BMI >= 25)
measures.action: Screen with fasting plasma glucose, HbA1c, or oral glucose tolerance test; offer/refer prediabetes to preventive interventions
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes: Screening (2021)
measures.appliesReason: Age 43 in 35-70 band AND BMI just crossed 25 (overweight) -> risk gate now met. Eligibility is newly triggered by the BMI threshold.
measures.notes: Grade B. Risk-gated: requires overweight/obesity (BMI>=25, or >=23 in Asian American persons per the rec). Patient's BMI just crossed 25, so he now QUALIFIES -- this is a newly activated measure. USPSTF states screening every 3 years may be reasonable for those with normal initial results. (Note: ADA screens more broadly from age 35 regardless of BMI -- authority disagreement.)

measures.title: Hypertension (high blood pressure) screening
measures.population: Adults 18 years or older
measures.action: Screen with office blood pressure measurement (OBPM), with out-of-office confirmation before diagnosis
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertension in adults 18 years or older with office blood pressure measurement (OBPM). The USPSTF recommends obtaining blood pressure measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Hypertension in Adults: Screening (2021)
measures.appliesReason: Age 43 (>=40) -> annual screening recommended per USPSTF interval guidance.
measures.notes: Grade A. USPSTF suggests annual screening for adults >=40 (and those at increased risk); every 3-5 years for ages 18-39 not at increased risk with prior normal reading. Patient is 43 -> annual. Diagnosis requires out-of-office confirmation (ABPM/HBPM).

measures.title: Depression screening (adults)
measures.population: Adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons and older adults
measures.action: Screen for depression with adequate systems for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends screening for depression in the adult population, including pregnant and postpartum persons.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023)
measures.appliesReason: Universal adult recommendation; age 43 qualifies. No risk gate.
measures.notes: Grade B (depression). NOTE: in the same 2023 statement, screening for SUICIDE RISK in adults is Grade I (insufficient evidence) -- do not conflate. USPSTF found no evidence on optimal screening interval; pragmatic approach is to screen those not previously screened and use clinical judgment for repeat screening.

measures.title: Unhealthy alcohol use screening and brief counseling
measures.population: Adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women, in primary care settings
measures.action: Screen for unhealthy alcohol use (e.g., AUDIT-C, SASQ); provide brief behavioral counseling to those with risky/hazardous drinking
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends screening for unhealthy alcohol use in primary care settings in adults 18 years or older, including pregnant women, and providing persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking with brief behavioral counseling interventions to reduce unhealthy alcohol use.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018)
measures.appliesReason: Universal adult recommendation; age 43 qualifies. No risk gate.
measures.notes: Grade B for adults. (Adolescents 12-17 are Grade I.) USPSTF does not specify a screening interval.

measures.title: Tobacco use screening and cessation interventions (adults)
measures.population: All adults (nonpregnant adults who use tobacco for pharmacotherapy)
measures.action: Ask all adults about tobacco use, advise to stop, provide behavioral interventions and FDA-approved pharmacotherapy to users
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all adults about tobacco use, advise them to stop using tobacco, and provide behavioral interventions and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved pharmacotherapy for cessation to nonpregnant adults who use tobacco.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Tobacco Smoking Cessation in Adults, Including Pregnant Persons: Interventions (2021)
measures.appliesReason: The ASK/screening component (Grade A) applies to ALL adults including this never-smoker; clinicians should ask all adults about tobacco use. The advise/pharmacotherapy components only trigger for tobacco users.
measures.notes: Grade A. IMPORTANT for this lifelong never-smoker: the 'ask about tobacco use' screening step still applies to everyone; only the cessation intervention/pharmacotherapy steps are conditional on being a current user. So the screening measure is satisfied by documenting never-smoker status; no cessation intervention indicated. USPSTF sets no formal interval; asking at visits is standard.

measures.title: Lung cancer screening (low-dose CT)
measures.population: Adults aged 50 to 80 years with >=20 pack-year history who currently smoke or quit within past 15 years
measures.riskCondition: ever-smoker >=20 pack-years AND (current smoker OR quit <15 years ago)
measures.action: Annual screening with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT)
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung cancer with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoking history and currently smoke or have quit within the past 15 years.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Lung Cancer: Screening (2021)
measures.appliesReason: Lifelong never-smoker -> 0 pack-years, fails the >=20 pack-year smoking-history gate. Also below age 50. Smoking gate alone excludes.
measures.notes: Grade B. EXCLUDED for this patient: never-smoker (0 pack-years) does not meet the smoking-history requirement, and he is also below the 50-year minimum age. Will never qualify on smoking grounds as a lifelong never-smoker.

measures.title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) screening
measures.population: Men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked (B); never-smoked men selective (C)
measures.action: One-time screening with ultrasonography
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends 1-time screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) with ultrasonography in men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Screening (2019)
measures.appliesReason: Lifelong never-smoker and age 43. The Grade B (ever-smoked) gate fails; he is far below the 65-year minimum age. As a never-smoked man he would at most fall under Grade C (selective) at 65-75, not routine.
measures.notes: Grade B for ever-smoked men 65-75; Grade C (selectively offer) for never-smoked men 65-75; Grade D against routine screening in never-smoked women without family history; Grade I for women 65-75 who ever smoked or have family history. This 43yo never-smoker: well below age and not an ever-smoker. If/when he reaches 65-75 he would fall under Grade C (clinician selectively offers) given never-smoker status, NOT routine Grade B.

measures.title: Influenza vaccination (annual)
measures.population: All adults 19 years and older; 1 dose annually each influenza season
measures.action: Administer 1 dose of any influenza vaccine appropriate for age and health status each year
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Influenza (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: 1 dose any influenza vaccine appropriate for age and health status annually
measures.appliesReason: routine by age for all adults 19+; this 43yo needs it annually
measures.notes: Routine-by-age. No brand preference at age 43 (preferential HD-IIV3/RIV3/aIIV3 products apply only at 65+).

measures.title: COVID-19 vaccination
measures.population: All adults 19 years and older; stay up to date with current season formulation
measures.action: Unvaccinated adults 19-64: 1 dose 2024-25 Moderna or Pfizer-BioNTech, or 2 doses 2024-25 Novavax at 0 and 3-8 weeks
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — COVID-19 (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Ages 19-64 years (unvaccinated): 1 dose 2024-25 Moderna or Pfizer-BioNTech, or 2 doses 2024-25 Novavax at 0, 3-8 weeks
measures.appliesReason: routine by age for all adults 19+; 43yo should stay up to date with current formulation
measures.notes: Routine-by-age; dosing depends on prior vaccination history and current season's formulation. The added 6-month second dose applies at 65+, not at 43.

measures.title: Tdap / Td (tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis)
measures.population: All adults: 1 dose Tdap (if not previously received as adult), then Td or Tdap booster every 10 years
measures.action: Ensure a one-time adult Tdap dose, then a Td or Tdap booster every 10 years
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule by Age — Tdap/Td (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: 1 dose Tdap, then Td or Tdap booster every 10 years
measures.appliesReason: routine by age; 43yo needs one-time Tdap then 10-year boosters
measures.notes: Routine-by-age. One-time adult Tdap plus 10-year (120-month) Td/Tdap booster cycle; additional Tdap each pregnancy (not applicable to a male).

measures.title: Hepatitis B vaccination (universal adults 19-59)
measures.population: All adults aged 19 through 59 years (universal, no risk-factor screening required); 60+ with risk factors or by choice
measures.action: Complete a 2-, 3-, or 4-dose HepB series
measures.citationTitle: Universal Hepatitis B Vaccination in Adults Aged 19-59 Years: Updated ACIP Recommendations — United States, 2022 (MMWR 71;13)
measures.ruleQuote: Age 19 through 59 years: complete a 2- or 3- or 4-dose series
measures.appliesReason: age 43 falls inside the 2022 universal 19-59 band; no risk assessment needed
measures.notes: Since 2022 ACIP recommends HepB universally for ALL adults 19-59 regardless of risk; at 60+ it becomes risk-based or patient choice. This 43yo qualifies on age alone.

measures.title: Hepatitis A vaccination
measures.population: Adults at risk (e.g., travel to endemic areas, MSM, drug use, chronic liver disease, homelessness) OR any adult requesting protection
measures.action: Complete a 2-dose HepA series (or 3-4 dose combination HepA-HepB schedule)
measures.riskCondition: risk indication (travel, MSM, drug use, chronic liver disease, homelessness) or patient request
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Hepatitis A (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Any person who is not fully vaccinated and requests vaccination...complete 2-dose series HepA
measures.appliesReason: no risk indication established for this average-risk 43yo; applies only if risk factor/travel or patient requests
measures.notes: Risk/travel-based, but ACIP also allows any adult to receive it on request even without a risk factor.

measures.title: HPV vaccination
measures.population: Routine catch-up through age 26; ages 27-45 by shared clinical decision-making
measures.action: Complete a 2- or 3-dose series (3 doses when initiated at 15+); ages 27-45 only after shared clinical decision-making
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — HPV (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Adults age 27-45 years: Based on shared clinical decision-making, complete a 2- or 3-dose series
measures.appliesReason: age 43 is past the routine-through-26 window but inside the 27-45 shared-clinical-decision-making band
measures.notes: Not routine at 43. ACIP says it is NOT routinely recommended 27-45; offer only after a shared decision weighing likely new exposures. 3 doses since initiated after age 15.

measures.title: Zoster (recombinant, RZV/Shingrix)
measures.population: All immunocompetent adults 50 years and older; immunocompromised adults 19 years and older
measures.action: 2-dose RZV series (doses 2-6 months apart; 1-2 months apart if immunocompromised)
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Zoster (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Age 50 years or older: 2-dose series recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix)
measures.appliesReason: routine RZV starts at age 50; this 43yo immunocompetent patient becomes eligible in ~2032 (age 50)
measures.notes: Routine-by-age at 50. Would apply now only if the patient had an immunocompromising condition (RZV recommended 19+ in that case, MMWR 71;3).

measures.title: Pneumococcal vaccination
measures.population: Adults 19-49 only if they have a chronic medical or immunocompromising risk condition; routine for all adults 50+
measures.action: 1 dose PCV15, PCV20, or PCV21 (if PCV15 used, follow with PPSV23 >=1 year later)
measures.riskCondition: chronic heart/lung/liver disease, diabetes, alcoholism, smoking, CSF leak, cochlear implant, asplenia, or immunocompromise
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Pneumococcal (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: 1 dose PCV15 or 1 dose PCV20 or 1 dose PCV21; if PCV15 is used, administer 1 dose PPSV23 at least 1 year after
measures.appliesReason: at age 43 pneumococcal is risk-gated; applies only with a qualifying chronic/immunocompromising condition (none established) — becomes routine at 50
measures.notes: Risk-based in the 19-49 band; ACIP lowered the routine age-based threshold to 50 (Oct 2024). For an average-risk 43yo with no listed condition, not indicated yet.

measures.title: RSV vaccination
measures.population: All adults 75 years and older; adults 50-74 at increased risk of severe RSV disease
measures.action: 1 dose of an RSV vaccine (Arexvy, Abrysvo, or mResvia)
measures.riskCondition: age 75+ (universal) OR age 50-74 with increased-risk condition (chronic heart/lung disease, diabetes on insulin, immunocompromise, severe obesity, etc.)
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — RSV (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Age 75 years or older: Unvaccinated: 1 dose. Age 50-74 years: Unvaccinated and at increased risk of severe RSV disease: 1 dose
measures.appliesReason: youngest RSV eligibility is age 50 (and only if high-risk); this 43yo is below the age gate entirely
measures.notes: Age 43 is below all RSV age gates. ACIP lowered the high-risk threshold from 60 to 50 in 2025; universal at 75+. Not applicable for several years.

measures.title: MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) evidence of immunity
measures.population: Adults born in 1957 or later without acceptable evidence of immunity
measures.action: Ensure 1 or 2 doses of MMR (1 dose for routine adult immunity; 2 doses for high-risk groups e.g., healthcare personnel, students, international travelers)
measures.riskCondition: born 1957 or later AND lacking documented immunity (vaccination record, lab evidence, or disease)
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — MMR (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Born before 1957...documentation of receipt of MMR vaccine, laboratory evidence of immunity or disease
measures.appliesReason: born 1982 (after 1957) so NOT presumed immune by birth year; needs documented immunity — 1 dose if none, more if a high-risk indication
measures.notes: Birth-cohort logic: born 1957 or later is NOT presumed immune. Acceptable evidence = documented MMR doses, lab immunity, or disease. 2 doses only if a high-risk indication (e.g., travel, healthcare work) applies.

measures.title: Varicella (chickenpox) evidence of immunity
measures.population: Adults without evidence of immunity; U.S.-born before 1980 may be presumed immune (except certain groups)
measures.action: Ensure 2 doses of varicella-containing vaccine at least 4 weeks apart if no other evidence of immunity
measures.riskCondition: lacks evidence of immunity (born 1980 or later is NOT presumed immune by birth year)
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Varicella (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: U.S.-born before 1980...documentation of 2 doses varicella-containing vaccine at least 4 weeks apart
measures.appliesReason: born 1982 (1980 or later) so the born-before-1980 presumption does NOT apply; needs documented immunity or a 2-dose series
measures.notes: Key birth-cohort distinction: the 'born before 1980' presumption of immunity does NOT cover this 1982 patient. Verify history of disease, lab immunity, or 2 documented doses; otherwise vaccinate.

measures.title: Meningococcal ACWY (MenACWY)
measures.population: Adults with risk indications (asplenia/sickle cell, persistent complement deficiency, complement inhibitor use, HIV, microbiologists, travel to/residence in hyperendemic areas, outbreak)
measures.action: 1 or 2 doses MenACWY depending on indication, with boosters every 5 years while risk persists
measures.riskCondition: asplenia, persistent complement component deficiency, complement inhibitor use, HIV, travel to meningitis belt/Hajj, microbiologist, outbreak
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Meningococcal ACWY (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Anatomical or functional asplenia (including sickle cell disease), HIV infection, persistent complement component deficiency
measures.appliesReason: purely risk-based; no qualifying medical/exposure/travel indication established for this 43yo
measures.notes: Risk-based at any adult age. Also indicated for certain travel (meningitis belt, Hajj) — overlaps with the travel-vaccine set.

measures.title: Meningococcal B (MenB)
measures.population: Adults with risk indications (asplenia/sickle cell, persistent complement deficiency, complement inhibitor use, microbiologists, outbreak); routine SCDM only at 16-23
measures.action: 2- or 3-dose MenB series depending on product and indication, with boosters while risk persists
measures.riskCondition: asplenia, persistent complement component deficiency, complement inhibitor use, microbiologist, outbreak
measures.citationTitle: Adult Immunization Schedule Notes — Meningococcal B (CDC/ACIP, 2025)
measures.ruleQuote: Anatomical or functional asplenia (including sickle cell disease), persistent complement component deficiency, complement inhibitor use
measures.appliesReason: risk-based at 43; the age-16-23 shared-decision option does not apply, and no risk condition is established
measures.notes: The shared-clinical-decision-making MenB option is for ages 16-23 only; at 43 MenB is purely risk-indication driven.

measures.title: Yellow fever vaccine (travel)
measures.population: Travelers to / residents of areas with risk of yellow fever virus transmission (parts of sub-Saharan Africa and tropical South America); may be required for entry
measures.action: Single dose of live-attenuated yellow fever vaccine (YF-VAX) at least 10 days before travel; generally lifelong
measures.riskCondition: travel to/residence in a yellow-fever-endemic area, or country entry requirement
measures.citationTitle: CDC Yellow Book — Vaccination and Immunoprophylaxis, General Principles (Travel)
measures.ruleQuote: Yellow fever vaccine is recommended for travelers to areas with risk of yellow fever virus transmission and may be required for entry.
measures.appliesReason: travel-based only; no endemic-area travel established for this 43yo
measures.notes: Travel/required-for-entry vaccine; one lifetime dose now considered protective for most travelers. Must be given at a designated YF vaccination center.

measures.title: Typhoid vaccine (travel)
measures.population: Travelers to areas of endemic typhoid (e.g., South Asia and other regions), and certain lab workers/household contacts of carriers
measures.action: Oral Ty21a (4 capsules, boost every 5 years) or injectable Vi polysaccharide (1 dose, boost every 2 years)
measures.riskCondition: travel to typhoid-endemic region, lab exposure, or household contact of a chronic carrier
measures.citationTitle: CDC Yellow Book — Typhoid (Travel Vaccines)
measures.ruleQuote: Injectable typhoid vaccine requires a booster every 2 years; oral typhoid vaccine boosters are recommended every 5 years for those at continued risk.
measures.appliesReason: travel-based only; no endemic-area travel established for this 43yo
measures.notes: Travel-based; booster interval differs by formulation (oral every 5 yr, injectable every 2 yr).

measures.title: Cholera vaccine (travel)
measures.population: Adults 18-64 traveling to an area of active toxigenic Vibrio cholerae O1 transmission
measures.action: Single dose of live-attenuated oral cholera vaccine (CVD 103-HgR / Vaxchora) at least 10 days before travel
measures.riskCondition: travel to an area of active cholera (toxigenic V. cholerae O1) transmission
measures.citationTitle: CDC Yellow Book — Cholera (Travel Vaccines)
measures.ruleQuote: ACIP recommends a single-dose, live attenuated oral cholera vaccine (CVD 103-HgR) for travelers to an area with active toxigenic Vibrio cholerae O1 transmission, given at least 10 days before travel.
measures.appliesReason: travel-based only; no active-transmission-area travel established for this 43yo (who is within the 18-64 product age range)
measures.notes: Travel-based; the licensed oral cholera vaccine is approved for ages 2-64, so this 43yo is age-eligible if traveling to an active transmission area.

measures.title: Rabies vaccine, pre-exposure (travel/occupational)
measures.population: People at risk of rabies exposure: certain travelers to enzootic areas with limited rabies-care access, and occupational risk groups (veterinarians, lab workers, animal handlers)
measures.action: 2-dose pre-exposure prophylaxis series on days 0 and 7; titer checks/boosters for ongoing risk
measures.riskCondition: occupational rabies exposure or travel to a rabies-enzootic area with poor access to post-exposure care
measures.citationTitle: CDC Yellow Book / ACIP — Rabies Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (Travel)
measures.ruleQuote: In 2022, ACIP approved a 2-dose pre-exposure rabies vaccination regimen given on days 0 and 7.
measures.appliesReason: risk/travel/occupational only; no rabies-exposure risk established for this 43yo
measures.notes: Travel/occupational. 2022 ACIP simplified pre-exposure prophylaxis to a 2-dose (day 0, 7) regimen with risk-based titer/booster follow-up.

measures.title: Japanese encephalitis vaccine (travel)
measures.population: People moving to a JE-endemic country, longer-term (>=1 month) travelers to endemic areas, and frequent/higher-risk shorter-term travelers during transmission season
measures.action: 2-dose inactivated Vero-cell JE vaccine (Ixiaro) on days 0 and 28; booster if continued risk after 1 year
measures.riskCondition: relocation to or >=1-month / frequent / higher-risk travel in a JE-endemic area during transmission season
measures.citationTitle: CDC Yellow Book — Japanese Encephalitis (Travel)
measures.ruleQuote: ACIP recommends JE vaccine for people moving to a JE-endemic country, longer-term (e.g., >=1 month) travelers to JE-endemic areas, and frequent travelers to JE-endemic areas.
measures.appliesReason: travel-based only; no qualifying JE-endemic travel established for this 43yo
measures.notes: Travel-based; explicitly NOT recommended for very low-risk itineraries (short urban trips or travel outside transmission season).

measures.title: Screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in asymptomatic adults (ADA)
measures.population: All adults beginning at age 35 regardless of BMI or risk; plus adults of any age with overweight/obesity (BMI >=25, or >=23 in Asian-ancestry individuals) and one or more diabetes risk factors.
measures.action: Screen (test) for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes using FPG, 2-h plasma glucose during 75-g OGTT, or A1C.
measures.appliesReason: eligible on age alone: patient is 43, which is >=35, so ADA recommends screening regardless of BMI/risk
measures.ruleQuote: For all other people, screening should begin at age 35 years. ... repeat screening recommended at a minimum of 3-year intervals is reasonable, sooner with symptoms or change in risk (e.g., weight gain).
measures.citationTitle: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl 1):S27 (Recommendations 2.12a-2.12c)
measures.notes: ADA isn't graded on the USPSTF A-D/I scale, so grade is empty (ADA uses A/B/C/E evidence levels). KEY DIVERGENCE from USPSTF: USPSTF (2021) gates diabetes/prediabetes screening on overweight/obesity (BMI>=25) in adults 35-70; ADA recommends UNIVERSAL screening at age 35 for ALL adults regardless of BMI or risk (rec 2.12b), and additionally screens younger adults with overweight/obesity + risk factors (rec 2.12a). For THIS 43yo never-smoker average-risk male, ADA would have recommended screening starting at age 35 (8 years ago) on age alone, well before the USPSTF criterion was met — his BMI only recently crossed 25, so under USPSTF he became eligible only recently, whereas ADA-eligibility was triggered years earlier. Rescreen every 3 years (36 months) if normal, sooner with symptoms or weight gain. Acceptable tests: FPG, 2-h PG during 75-g OGTT, or A1C. Verbatim text retrieved from the diabetesjournals.org NIH PMC mirror (PMC12690183); canonical citation URL is the diabetesjournals.org article (direct fetch 403s behind publisher access controls).

measures.title: Lipid measurement / ASCVD risk assessment
measures.population: Adults 40 to 75 years with >=1 CVD risk factor; lipids measured to estimate 10-year ASCVD risk
measures.action: Measure lipids and estimate 10-year CVD risk (ACC/AHA Pooled Cohort Equations); offer statin per risk
measures.ruleQuote: The USPSTF recommends that clinicians prescribe a statin for the primary prevention of CVD for adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more CVD risk factors ... and an estimated 10-year risk of a cardiovascular event of 10% or greater.
measures.citationTitle: USPSTF Recommendation: Statin Use for the Primary Prevention of CVD in Adults (2022)
measures.appliesReason: Age 43 within 40-75; lipids measured periodically for ASCVD risk. Latest panel shows rising triglycerides / low HDL.
measures.notes: USPSTF has no standalone 'screen all adults' lipid grade; lipids are obtained to assess ASCVD risk for statin decisions. ACC/AHA suggests reassessing risk every 4-6 years; Epic's HM uses a 5-year interval.
